question.text: An electron in Hydrogen atom jumps from the second Bohr orbit to the ground state and the difference between the energies of the two states is radiated in the form of a photon. This photon strikes a material. If the work function of the material is 4.2 eV , then the stopping potential is (Energy of electron in n -th orbit $=-\frac{13.6}{\mathrm{n}^2} \mathrm{eV}$ )

solution.text:
Energy of photon emitted from hydrogen atom
$=-13.6\left[\frac{1}{2^2}-\frac{1}{1^2}\right]=10.2 \mathrm{eV}$

Now using Einstein's photoelectric equation.
$\begin{aligned}
& 10.2 \mathrm{eV}=4.2 \mathrm{eV}+\mathrm{eV}_{\mathrm{s}} \\
& \therefore \mathrm{~V}_{\mathrm{s}}=6 \text { Volt. }
\end{aligned}$
